intervals.label: first TPC module under construction
intervals.note: Start is the date of the design paper (arXiv v1, 27 October 2016), which says the first module is under construction. A November 2023 status paper says 'The construction of the detector was completed. The detector will be installed at the CJPL-II after the performance test in Shanghai.' No later source was found on installation; the PandaX website (checked 2026-10-26) calls PandaX-III 'a R&D effort to develop a high pressure gaseous Xenon TPC'. The status 'construction' is therefore the last documented stage, not a statement about 2026.
intervals.quote: The first 200 kg module is under construction and is expected to be deployed in the next 2-3 years.

placements.note: Planned placement: as of the November 2023 status paper the final detector was still to be installed at CJPL-II after tests in Shanghai; the 2016 design paper names CJPL without the phase.
placements.quote: The detector will be installed at the CJPL-II [17] after the performance test in Shanghai.

isotope.quote: It can hold about 140 kg of xenon (90% enriched) at an operating pressure of 10 bar.

module_count.quote: A tessellation of 52 20.0 × 20.0 cm2 thermal-bonding Micromegas modules [13, 14] are used for charge readout.

target_mass.quote: It can hold about 140 kg of xenon (90% enriched) at an operating pressure of 10 bar.

summary.plain: A steel vessel holding xenon gas at ten times atmospheric pressure, with a plane of tiny gas-amplifier modules at each end that image the tracks of electrons from a decay.
summary.technical: Cylindrical TPC (height 120 cm, diameter 160 cm) in a stainless-steel high-pressure vessel; 52 thermal-bonding Micromegas modules with Ge-film resistive anode read the charge; electric-field-shaping cage; 20 kg-scale prototype tested in Shanghai.

technology.quote: The PandaX-III experiment searches the neutrinoless double beta decay of 136 Xe with a high-pressure xenon gaseous time projection chamber (TPC). Thermalbonding Micromegas modules are used for charge collection.
technology.value: High-pressure gaseous xenon time projection chamber with thermal-bonding Micromegas charge-readout modules; tracks of the two electrons give topological background rejection
